items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: Charlie Parker and Art Tatum to me are the two that stand out for genius in this business.

ctx.x: It takes an awful lot of facility to pull that off.

Yes indeed it takes a lot of facility. And I was lucky because I had all that early, excellent training so I could do that. And Charlie Parker and Art Tatum to me are the two that stand out for genius in this business. Absolute genius. Everyone else, as good as they are — and this includes Oscar, and Oscar will tell you this, Oscar to me was the epitome of pianists — would tell you that the first, one of the innovators was Art Tatum. Nobody played like him before that. But after that everybody tried. Charlie…
Someone had a quote about that. If he could sue people for what they’ve taken from him.

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember doing a session with Art Tatum for Norman Granz... In fact, I wound up doing an album with Art Tatum

ctx.x: Right, interesting how it affected people…
Different people… Murphy:…effects people so differently…
Yeah. Murphy:…I mean, Charlie Parker and Art Tatum.
